[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **bracket** first: 74 − 23 = 51.

Group all **positive terms** and sum them: 91 + 51 + 64 + 35 = 241.

Subtract the **negative term**: 241 − 58 = 183.

**∴ The correct answer is 183.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 91 + (74 − 23) + 64 − 58 + 35

Using the **BODMAS** rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

⇒ 91 + 51 + 64 − 58 + 35

⇒ 142 + 64 − 58 + 35

⇒ 206 − 58 + 35

⇒ 148 + 35

⇒ 183

**∴ The correct answer is 183.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The **BODMAS** rule determines the sequence of mathematical operations to ensure consistent results: **B**rackets first, **O**rders (powers), then **D**ivision/**M**ultiplication, followed by **A**ddition/**S**ubtraction.

Addition and Subtraction Priority

Addition and subtraction are of the **same priority level** and can be performed from left to right or by grouping all positive and negative terms separately.

questions.question: Evaluate: [(0.86 ÷ 0.04)² + (3.5 + 0.5)³ ÷ (2.5 – 0.5)³] × 2
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve parts separately: (0.86 ÷ 0.04)² = 21.5² = 462.25.

For the ratio of cubes: (4³ ÷ 2³) = (4 ÷ 2)³ = 2³ = 8.

Total value within bracket = 462.25 + 8 = 470.25.

Final calculation: 470.25 × 2 = 940.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 940.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [(0.86 ÷ 0.04)² + (3.5 + 0.5)³ ÷ (2.5 − 0.5)³] × 2

**Method:** Apply the **BODMAS** rule to solve the operations in the correct sequence.

⇒ [(21.5)² + (4)³ ÷ (2)³] × 2

⇒ [462.25 + 64 ÷ 8] × 2

⇒ [462.25 + 8] × 2

⇒ 470.25 × 2

⇒ 940.5

**∴ The correct answer is 940.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The rule defines the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Orders** (Exponents/Roots), **Division** and **Multiplication** (left to right), and **Addition** and **Subtraction** (left to right).

Laws of Exponents

For any numbers a and b with exponent n, the property (aⁿ ÷ bⁿ) = (a ÷ b)ⁿ can be used to simplify calculations involving **squares** or **cubes**.

Decimal Division

When dividing decimals like 0.86 ÷ 0.04, multiply both the numerator and denominator by 100 to convert them into whole numbers (86 ÷ 4) before **evaluating**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the smallest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the **difference** between the **Denominator** and **Numerator** for each fraction.

For 10/11: 11 − 10 = 1 | For 11/12: 12 − 11 = 1 | For 7/8: 8 − 7 = 1 | For 13/14: 14 − 13 = 1.

When the **difference is constant**, the fraction with the **smallest numerator** is the smallest.

Comparing numerators 10, 11, 7, and 13, the smallest is 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Fractions are 10/11, 11/12, 7/8, and 13/14.

**Formula Used:** Converting fractions to **decimals** for direct comparison.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/872e44cfdd4395822d8a4232f8d6a9008c43d509d2fcdcd785aa8b1c4cafac38.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 10 ÷ 11 ≈ 0.909

⇒ 11 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.916

⇒ 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875

⇒ 13 ÷ 14 ≈ 0.928

Comparing the decimal values: 0.875 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proper Fractions Comparison

For **proper fractions** (numerator denominator) with the same difference, the rule is **reversed**: the fraction with the larger numerator is actually the smaller one.

questions.question: Which of the following lies between (13/6) & (9/4)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given fractions and options into **decimal values** for a quick comparison.

Given Range: 13/6 ≈ **2.167** and 9/4 = **2.25**.

Option 1: 31/14 ≈ **2.214** (Lies between 2.167 and 2.25).

Option 2: 15/7 ≈ 2.143 | Option 3: 19/8 = 2.375 | Option 4: 25/9 ≈ 2.778.

**∴ The correct answer is 31/14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two fractions 13/6 and 9/4.

**Formula Used:** To find a rational number between two fractions, we can equate denominators or compare their **numerical values**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/467b163d8e55e7dd3ddffd2381d12b77ad8b9b52a5c1f5f163f9fb38e1f9523f.png] 

⇒ **Lower Bound:** 13/6 = 2.1666...

⇒ **Upper Bound:** 9/4 = 2.25

⇒ Let us check **Option 1:** 31/14

⇒ 31 ÷ 14 ≈ 2.2142

⇒ Comparing values: 2.167 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Density Property of Rational Numbers

Between any two **rational numbers**, there exist infinitely many other rational numbers. A simple way to find one is the mean: (a + b) ÷ 2.

Comparing Fractions

To compare a/b and c/d, check the products **(a × d)** and **(b × c)**. If a × d > b × c, then a/b > c/d.

Common Denominator Method

Convert all fractions to a **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of their denominators to make direct comparison of numerators easier.

questions.question: frac{(sqrt{8}+sqrt{2})² + (sqrt{8}-sqrt{2})²}{60} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the algebraic identity: **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)**

Here, a = √8 and b = √2.

Numerator = 2((√8)² + (√2)²) = 2(8 + 2) = 2 × 10 = 20

Required value = 20 ÷ 60 = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** [(√8 + √2)² + (√8 − √2)²] ÷ 60

**Method:** Expanding the **squares** using (a ± b)² = a² + b² ± 2ab

⇒ First term: (√8 + √2)² = (√8)² + (√2)² + 2(√8 × √2)

⇒ 8 + 2 + 2√16 = 10 + 2(4) = 18

⇒ Second term: (√8 − √2)² = (√8)² + (√2)² − 2(√8 × √2)

⇒ 8 + 2 − 2√16 = 10 − 2(4) = 2

⇒ Expression = (18 + 2) ÷ 60

⇒ 20 ÷ 60 = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Sum

The formula **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)** simplifies calculations where the middle terms (+2ab and −2ab) cancel out.

Algebraic Identity for Difference

The formula **(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab** is used when the squared terms (a² and b²) cancel out.

Simplifying Surds

Numbers under a square root can be simplified if they have perfect square factors, e.g., **√8 = √(4 × 2) = 2√2**.

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is 54 square cm. The length of the rectangle is 6 cm. What is the breadth (in cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **Rectangle**, the relationship between **Area**, **Length**, and **Breadth** is **Area** = **Length** × **Breadth**.

Given **Area** = 54 cm² and **Length** = 6 cm.

**Breadth** = 54 ÷ 6 = 9 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of the **Rectangle** = 54 cm²

**Length** (l) of the **Rectangle** = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Area** of **Rectangle** = **Length** × **Breadth**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b665bad1c1c281cbe11bc0c5ec664a157b45814826b3d88bcda48da5c954ff6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Area** = **Length** × **Breadth**

⇒ 54 = 6 × **Breadth**

⇒ **Breadth** = 54 ÷ 6

⇒ **Breadth** = 9 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of Rectangle

The **Perimeter** is the total boundary length, calculated as P = 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The **Diagonal** (d) connects opposite corners and is found using Pythagoras theorem: d = √(Length² + Breadth²).

Square Property

A **Square** is a special rectangle where **Length** equals **Breadth**, so **Area** = Side².

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is 80 square cm. The length of the rectangle is 10 cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Breadth** = Area ÷ Length = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 cm

**Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

**Perimeter** = 2 × (10 + 8) = 2 × 18 = 36 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of the rectangle = 80 cm²

**Length** of the rectangle = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area = **Length** × **Breadth**

Perimeter = 2 × (**Length** + **Breadth**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d3e56541d11af462b1324e1e4b36bf518206f3d8801020c459b7cb0b55c8098.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = Length × Breadth

⇒ 80 = 10 × Breadth

⇒ Breadth = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 cm

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (10 + 8)

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × 18

⇒ Perimeter = 36 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The diagonal d of a rectangle with length L and breadth B is calculated using the Pythagoras theorem: d = √(L² + B²).

Relationship with Square

A square is a special type of rectangle where Length = Breadth. Its **Area** = side² and **Perimeter** = 4 × side.

Units of Measurement

Area is always expressed in **square units** (cm², m²), while perimeter and diagonal are expressed in **linear units** (cm, m).

questions.question: Average of 11 numbers is 6. Each number becomes 5 times of itself. What will be the new average of the numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each observation in a data set is **multiplied** by a constant value **k**, the **new average** is also multiplied by the same constant **k**.

Old Average = 6

Constant factor (k) = 5

New Average = 6 × 5 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 11 numbers = 6

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0e0e330ec6d6790e5591269b7ce8490528c42ff8a07b1f04b9703b91d9c4b89.png] 

⇒ Sum of 11 numbers = Average × Total numbers

⇒ Original Sum = 6 × 11 = 66

⇒ Since each number is multiplied by 5, the **New Sum** = 66 × 5 = 330

⇒ New Average = New Sum ÷ Total numbers

⇒ New Average = 330 ÷ 11 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Addition/Subtraction on Average

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from each observation, the new average will be (Old Average + **k**) or (Old Average − **k**) respectively.

Effect of Division on Average

If each observation is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the new average becomes (Old Average ÷ **k**).

Average of First n Natural Numbers

The average of the first **n** natural numbers is given by the formula: (n + 1) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The average age of 11 persons is 15 years. If the age of 12th persons is added, then the average remains same. What is the age (in years) of the 12th person?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **average remains same** even after adding a new person, the value of the **new person** must be **equal** to the original **average**.

Initial Average = 15 years

Since the average of 12 persons remains 15 years, the age of the 12th person is exactly 15 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average age of 11 persons = 15 years | Average age of 12 persons = 15 years.

**Formula:** Total Age = Average × Number of persons

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca84f2f1095eb82007d226aa8a972983ab529aefce90f3861a2ae46eba98ac35.png] 

⇒ Total age of 11 persons = 11 × 15 = 165 years

⇒ Total age of 12 persons = 12 × 15 = 180 years

⇒ Age of 12th person = Total age (12 persons) − Total age (11 persons)

⇒ Age of 12th person = 180 − 165 = 15 years

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Adding a Value on Average

If the added value is greater than the average, the new average increases; if less, it decreases; if equal, the average remains **constant**.

Net Deviation Method

New Value = New Average + (Old Count × Change in Average). Here, Change = 0, so New Value = New Average = 15.

Average Formula

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations.

questions.question: The greatest possible length (in cm) which can be used to measure exactly the lengths 6 metres, 2 metres 70 cm, 11 metres 20 cm is ______.
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Convert all lengths to **cm**: 600, 270, and 1120. The **greatest measuring length** is the **HCF** of these values. By inspection, all numbers end in 0, so **10** is a common factor. Remaining values: 60, 27, and 112. Since 27 (3³) and 112 (2⁴ × 7) have no common prime factors, the HCF is 10. **∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

questions.question: 7 kg of water is mixed in 21 kg of milk. What is the percentage of water in the mixture?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of **Water** to **Milk** = 7 : 21 = 1 : 3 Total units in **mixture** = 1 + 3 = 4 units **Percentage of water** = (Water units ÷ Total units) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25% **∴ The correct answer is 25 percent.**

questions.question: Cost price of an article is Rs. 6000. The loss percentage is 20 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Loss** = 20% = 1/5 → Ratio of **CP : SP** = 5 : (5 − 1) = 5 : 4

Given, 5 units (CP) = ₹6000

∴ 1 unit = 6000 ÷ 5 = ₹1200

∴ **Selling Price** = 4 units = 4 × ₹1200 = ₹4800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the article = ₹6000

**Loss Percentage** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/205c7fc2820173c9d86a48fd5b66e2d9b3aebd55243a78f713d9fee5d65b5fea.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 6000 × (100 − 20) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 6000 × 80 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 60 × 80

⇒ SP = ₹4800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Calculation

Profit occurs when SP > CP, where Profit = SP − CP. Loss occurs when CP > SP, where Loss = CP − SP.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is the reduction offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Effective Percentage Change

For successive percentage changes of x% and y%, the total effective change is [x + y + (x × y)/100] %.

questions.question: A person donates 40 percent of his income and deposits 60 percent of the remainder in his bank. If the remaining amount is Rs. 10800 now, then what is the income of the person?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Income** be 100 units.

**Donation** = 40% of 100 = 40 units → **Remainder** = 60 units.

**Bank Deposit** = 60% of 60 = 36 units → **Final Remainder** = 60 − 36 = 24 units.

Given: 24 units = Rs. 10800.

1 unit = 10800 ÷ 24 = 450.

Income = 100 units = 100 × 450 = Rs. 45000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 45000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Donation Percentage = 40%

Bank Deposit of Remainder = 60%

Final Remaining Amount = Rs. 10800

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09bcddc2e572d7501f2cf701ee8bdf4960ed6d4253bb88d081c04954daf75325.png] 

Let the **total income** of the person be **x**.

⇒ Amount after donation = x − (40/100)x = 60/100 × x

⇒ Amount after bank deposit = (60/100 × x) × (100 − 60)/100

⇒ Final Remaining Amount = (60/100 × x) × 40/100

⇒ 10800 = (3/5) × (2/5) × x

⇒ 10800 = 6/25 × x

⇒ x = (10800 × 25) ÷ 6

⇒ x = 1800 × 25

⇒ x = 45000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 45000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

If a value is changed by a% and then the remaining by b%, the effective final value is original value × (1 − a/100) × (1 − b/100).

Percentage Change

To calculate the percentage of a part from the whole: (Part ÷ Whole) × 100.

Base Change in Percentage

When calculating 60% of the remainder, the "base" shifts from the original income to the remainder amount after the first deduction.

questions.question: The ratio of selling price of an article to the cost price of the article is 6 : 5. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given the ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** = 6 : 5.

Assume **CP** = 5 units and **SP** = 6 units.

**Profit** = SP − CP = 6 − 5 = 1 unit.

**Profit %** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** = 6 : 5

**Formula Used:**

**Profit percentage** = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fd8e96f47301c9182294d311485affbd682b1542c59d499c328de0abce74c9c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price** be 5x and the **Selling Price** be 6x.

⇒ **Profit** = Selling Price − Cost Price

⇒ Profit = 6x − 5x = x

⇒ **Profit %** = (x ÷ 5x) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When CP > SP, a loss is incurred. **Loss %** = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. **SP** = MP − Discount.

CP Calculation from Profit%

If SP and Profit% are known, **CP** = [SP ÷ (100 + Profit%)] × 100.

questions.question: A, B and C working alone can complete a work in 28, 35 and 42 days respectively. In how many days A, B and C together can complete 3/7 part of the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 28, 35, and 42 = 420 (**Total Work**).

Efficiency of **A** = 15, **B** = 12, **C** = 10.

Combined efficiency of **A + B + C** = 37 units/day.

Work to be completed = 3/7 × 420 = 180 units.

Time taken = 180 ÷ 37 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 180/37 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 28 days, **B** = 35 days, and **C** = 42 days.

**Formula Used:** **Total Work** = **Efficiency** × **Time**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of **A**, **B**, and **C** = 15 + 12 + 10 = 37 units/day.

⇒ Required work to be completed = 3/7 × 420 = 180 units.

⇒ Time required by all three together = **Work** ÷ **Combined Efficiency**

⇒ Time = 180 ÷ 37 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 180/37 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their **individual efficiencies** are added to find the **net efficiency** of the group.

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a specific task (Efficiency = 1/Time).

Work Fraction Formula

If 1/n of the work is to be done, the time taken is (Total Work × 1/n) ÷ **Total Efficiency**.

questions.question: X alone can do a work in 18 days. Y alone can do the same work in 27 days. Z alone can do the same work in 54 days. All three together complete the work. Wages received by X out of total wages received by X, Y and Z are Rs. 7200. What is the absolute difference (in Rs.) between the total wages of Y and Z and total wages of X and Z?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **efficiency** X : Y : Z = 1/18 : 1/27 : 1/54 = 3 : 2 : 1

**Wage of X** (3 units) = ₹7200 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹2400

Required **Difference** = |(Y + Z) − (X + Z)| = |Y − X|

Difference in units = |2 − 3| = 1 unit = ₹2400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by **X** = 18 days, **Y** = 27 days, **Z** = 54 days.

Formula: **Efficiency** = **Total Work** ÷ **Time**; **Wage** ∝ **Efficiency** (if time is constant).

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 X
 18
 54 (LCM of 18, 27, 54)
 3
 
 

 Y
 27
 2
 
 

 Z
 54
 1
 
 

⇒ Ratio of **efficiency** (and thus wages) X : Y : Z = 3 : 2 : 1

⇒ Given, **Wage of X** = 3 units = ₹7200

⇒ 1 unit = 7200 ÷ 3 = ₹2400

⇒ **Wage of Y** = 2 units = 2 × 2400 = ₹4800

⇒ **Wage of Z** = 1 unit = 1 × 2400 = ₹2400

⇒ Total wages of (**Y + Z**) = 4800 + 2400 = ₹7200

⇒ Total wages of (**X + Z**) = 7200 + 2400 = ₹9600

⇒ **Absolute difference** = |7200 − 9600| = ₹2400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Rule

Wages are distributed in the ratio of **Work Done**. If time spent is same for all, it simplifies to the ratio of their **efficiencies**.

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken (Efficiency = 1/Time) when the **total work** is constant.

LCM Method for Total Work

To simplify calculations, **Total Work** is assumed to be the **Least Common Multiple** (LCM) of the days taken by each person.

questions.question: The speed of a car is 50 km/hr for first 3 hours and 20 km/hr for the next 7 hours. What is the total distance (in km) covered by the car?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = (Speed₁ × Time₁) + (Speed₂ × Time₂)

Total Distance = (50 × 3) + (20 × 7)

Total Distance = 150 + 140 = 290 km

**∴ The correct answer is 290 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed₁** = 50 km/hr, **Time₁** = 3 hr

**Speed₂** = 20 km/hr, **Time₂** = 7 hr

**Formula:** **Distance = Speed × Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f235cc12e44e4c68c8cbc359d6da2c90a9e9cc45ee97e744ad90e0f55b99dd9.png] 

⇒ **Distance₁** = 50 × 3 = 150 km

⇒ **Distance₂** = 20 × 7 = 140 km

⇒ **Total Distance** = 150 + 140 = 290 km

**∴ The correct answer is 290 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

It is the total distance covered divided by the total time taken: Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Distance Formula

Distance (D) = Speed (S) × Time (T). If speed is constant, distance is directly proportional to time.

questions.question: A boat can row 25 km in 5 hours in still water. It can row 56 km downstream and 24 km upstream in total 19 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the stream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed of boat** in still water (u) = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 km/hr.

Let **stream speed** be v. Use option elimination in the equation: 56/(5 + v) + 24/(5 − v) = 19.

Try **v = 3** from the options:

56/(5 + 3) + 24/(5 − 3) = 56/8 + 24/2 = 7 + 12 = 19.

The equation is satisfied when **v = 3 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed of boat** in still water (u) = 25 km ÷ 5 hr = 5 km/hr.

**Total time** taken for downstream and upstream journeys = 19 hr.

**Formula Used:**

**Downstream Speed** (D) = u + v | **Upstream Speed** (U) = u − v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37e04af036ee064a1c189b0f6936e4a7e14c80911ef30f5d218324c85ffeb1c8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 56 / (5 + v) + 24 / (5 − v) = 19

⇒ [56(5 − v) + 24(5 + v)] / [(5 + v)(5 − v)] = 19

⇒ [280 − 56v + 120 + 24v] / [25 − v²] = 19

⇒ 400 − 32v = 19(25 − v²)

⇒ 400 − 32v = 475 − 19v²

⇒ 19v² − 32v − 75 = 0

⇒ 19v² − 57v + 25v − 75 = 0

⇒ 19v(v − 3) + 25(v − 3) = 0

⇒ (19v + 25)(v − 3) = 0

⇒ v = 3 or v = −25/19 (Speed cannot be negative)

⇒ v = 3 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speeds in Water

When rowing **downstream**, the speeds of the boat and stream add up. When rowing **upstream**, the stream speed is subtracted from the boat speed.

Speed Formulas

Speed of Boat in Still Water (u) = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2. Speed of Stream (v) = (Downstream − Upstream) ÷ 2.

Quadratic Roots Tip

In **Boats and Streams** problems, the quadratic equation usually has one positive and one negative root. Always pick the **positive value** as speed.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 160 percent of its cost price. Its selling price is 70 percent of the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Multiplier for **Selling Price** = 1.6 (Markup) × 0.7 (Discount factor)

SP = CP × (1.6 × 0.7) = CP × 1.12

**Profit Percentage** = (1.12 − 1) × 100 = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Marked Price (MP)** = 160% of **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** = 70% of MP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb9ce778e31aa35ffecc71ad08c3d5c5d616d00bf81bff9df9072512625e30b0.png] 

Assume the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article is ₹100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 160% of 100 = ₹160.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 70% of 160

⇒ SP = (70 ÷ 100) × 160

⇒ SP = 0.7 × 160 = ₹112.

⇒ **Profit** = Selling Price − Cost Price

⇒ Profit = 112 − 100 = ₹12.

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (12 ÷ 100) × 100 = 12%.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Formulas

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100. Always calculate on CP unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Discount

SP = MP × [1 − (Discount% ÷ 100)]. Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

Relationship between CP and MP

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). This formula directly links **markup** and **profit** with **discount**.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by a% and then b%, net change = [a + b + (ab ÷ 100)]%. For markup (+a) and discount (−b), the sign of b is negative.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 50 percent more than its cost price. What maximum discount percentage can be offered on this article so that there is no loss?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100. **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150. For **no loss**, the minimum **Selling Price (SP)** must be equal to the **CP**, which is 100. Maximum **Discount** = MP − SP = 150 − 100 = 50. **Max Discount %** = (50 ÷ 150) × 100 = 33.33%. **∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**
